transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-07-18
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Dr. Laura Chen (Sierra Medical), Michael Torres (CTO), Jamal Reed (Data Eng)

[00:00] Ava: hi everyone, thanks for joining. this is Ava from Redwood, and samir's here from our solutions team. how's it going?
[00:06] Michael: good, thanks. busy week, but excited to get this scoped.
[00:12] Dr. Chen: yeah thanks, looking forward. we want to be clear on how you'll measure quality for the POC.
[00:18] Samir: absolutely. today's goal is to align on success criteria, workload size for the bench, the exact bench tests (latency, cost, accuracy) and a plan for golden prompts and regression tests.
[00:27] Ava: quick agenda — success criteria, data and workloads, test harness, golden prompt set, hallucination/format checks, scoring approach, timeline. sound ok?
[00:34] Dr. Chen: yes. I'll start with our top-level success criteria so we're aligned.
[00:40] Dr. Chen: we have three main things: 1) functional accuracy on our structured extraction tasks (we expect >= 92% F1 on key fields), 2) hallucination rate below 2% on sampled outputs, and 3) latency p95 under 800ms for single-record inference. those are the bar for production but for POC we'll be a little flexible but want to see clear trends.
[01:05] Jamal: to add, we need strict output schema enforcement — if model returns stray fields or bad formatting it's a failure for us.
[01:12] Samir: got it. output schema enforcement can be a separate rule-based validator in the harness. for hallucination checks we usually do a combination of reference-based comparison and targeted negative prompts.
[01:22] Ava: with the sample size, how many records can you share? earlier you mentioned 500 de-identified records?
[01:28] Jamal: yeah we can get you 500 by end of next week, they'll be de-id'd and include target fields and edge cases.
[01:34] Michael: on workload sizing, our expected production footprint is ~50 qps at peak but for the POC we want to simulate realistic mixes: single-record inference (65%), batch summarization (20%), embeddings for search (15%).
[01:48] Samir: that's helpful. for the bench we'll define three profiles: single-record latency, medium batching throughput, and embedding throughput. we'll size tokens per request — single-record ~350 tokens, batch summarization 2-5 docs per request ~1200 tokens, embedding payloads ~512 tokens.
[02:05] Samir: we'll run runs on hosted Redwood models first to get baseline then show how Dedicated or quantized variants change cost/latency.
[02:12] Dr. Chen: can you show both cost and accuracy tradeoffs? we care about unit economics.
[02:16] Ava: yes we'll include cost per 1k tokens and cost per successful extraction. Samir will define the exact metrics.
[02:22] Samir: on scoring approach — propose a composite score: weighted metrics with accuracy F1 (60%), hallucination penalty (20%), schema/format compliance (10%), latency penalty (10%). we can adjust weights to match your priorities.
[02:36] Dr. Chen: that weight looks reasonable, maybe bump latency to 15% for our use-case.
[02:40] Jamal: and we want a clear pass/fail threshold e.g. composite score >= 85 for green.
[02:45] Ava: noted. we'll propose defaults and you can tweak.
[02:48] Michael: about golden prompts — how do you curate them?
[02:51] Samir: we typically create a set of 40-60 golden prompts that cover typical happy path, edge cases, and adversarial items. each has an expected structured output. golden prompts are used for regression checks between model versions.
[03:05] Dr. Chen: do you keep them static during the POC? we want to avoid overfitting to the golden set.
[03:10] Samir: good point. recommended approach: lock a stable golden set for regression (not touched) and have a separate dynamic test set for tuning. also we can keep a holdout set for final validation.
[03:20] Jamal: for hallucination detection we want both automated heuristics and manual review sampling. automated checks include entity mismatch, hallucination score thresholds, and fact-consistency tests when applicable.
[03:32] Ava: we'll include those checks in the harness. also, format checks: output must conform to JSON schema; any deviation flagged as fail and scored heavily.
[03:40] Dr. Chen: sounds good. what about edge-case handling — long clinical notes with truncated context?
[03:45] Samir: we'll profile sequence lengths and do tests at 512, 1024, and 2048 token windows to measure degradation and latency. we'll also test KV cache hit rates for conversational flows if you plan multi-turn.
[03:58] Michael: security note — if we go to Dedicated or Private, we need to discuss KMS integration and audit logs. can we get a SOC2 + KMS docs?
[04:06] Ava: yes, we'll attach SOC 2 summary and the KMS/HSM integration notes in the doc package.
[04:12] Dr. Chen: timeline? you mentioned a 3-week POC earlier — can you outline milestones?
[04:17] Samir: propose: week 0 (today to 1 week) — data handoff and template setup; week 1 — baseline runs on hosted models with golden prompts and initial metrics; week 2 — tuning and additional runs including quantized variants and dedicated config; week 3 — final run, results review, and go/no-go decision.
[04:33] Jamal: that aligns with our internal schedule. we can commit to handing over samples by 2026-07-24.
[04:39] Ava: great. about benchmark execution — we'll provide a reproducible harness (python repo) and config files. Samir: we'll include dockerized runner and a metrics dashboard.
[04:49] Samir: on regression tests: we will run the golden prompt suite on every candidate model and compare scores; regressions trigger flags and we can retro-analyze differences to figure out which prompt families regressed.
[05:00] Dr. Chen: how do you handle prompt-engineering drift? if we tune prompts heavily, we want to ensure the overall system generalizes.
[05:06] Samir: we separate prompt tuning from model changes. the golden set is static; any prompt tuning is validated against holdout sets. we also recommend documenting prompt templates in the repo.
[05:17] Michael: what about hallucination measured as "fabricated facts" vs "unsupported inference" — do you distinguish?
[05:22] Samir: yes — we categorize hallucinations: factual fabrications (claims about verifiable facts), hallucinated entities (made-up names/IDs), and format hallucinations (wrong json/schema). we score and weight them differently in the penalties.
[05:36] Dr. Chen: do you provide tooling to surface example hallucinations? that would be useful for our SMEs to label.
[05:41] Ava: yes we'll output failure buckets with example cases and link to a review sheet for SMEs.
[05:47] Jamal: any constraints on model access? can we run on-prem for the final run?
[05:51] Samir: for POC we'll run on hosted for speed. final validation can be run on Dedicated or Private if you want — that requires lead time for infra and KMS work.
[06:01] Michael: ok, good. can you share a sample eval template now?
[06:05] Ava: we'll send the template and a short handbook that explains the composite scoring, the exact metrics (precision/recall/F1 thresholds), hallucination heuristics, and the harness README.
[06:14] Dr. Chen: one more: we need reproducible seeds and versioning so we can trace regressions to model commits.
[06:19] Samir: we'll record model version ids, tokenizer versions, and random seeds in result metadata.
[06:24] Ava: recap — Redwood sends eval template, golden prompt seed set, SOC2/KMS notes by 2026-07-20. Sierra Medical sends 500 de-id samples by 2026-07-24. We run baseline week of 2026-07-27, follow-up review on 2026-08-06.
[06:40] Dr. Chen: yep, that's it. any blockers or open questions?
[06:44] Jamal: just internal approval for sample sharing but that should be fine.
[06:48] Michael: no more from me.
[06:50] Ava: thanks all, we'll email the package after the call.
[06:54] Dr. Chen: thanks, bye.

Notes on tests and scoring (readout after meeting):
- Golden prompts: 50 prompts across extraction, summarization, and edge-cases. Expect pass/fail per prompt plus normalized score.
- Regression tests: run golden suite nightly on candidate branch; flag >5% drop in composite score.
- Hallucination checks: automated heuristics + 5% manual review sampling.
- Format checks: strict JSON schema validation; any schema violation counted as fail and heavily penalized in composite score.
- Scoring approach: composite score with editable weights; default proposal accuracy 60%, hallucination penalty 20%, schema compliance 10%, latency 10%. Pass threshold proposed at 85.
- Benchmarks: single-record p95 latency, throughput under batching, embeddings throughput, cost per 1k tokens.

Attachments referenced: eval-template.xlsx (will be shared), golden-prompts.csv (sample), SOC2-summary.pdf, KMS-integration-notes.md, benchmark-config.yml

End of transcript.
